scenario.reasoning: Three weeks of brief lightheaded spells in a man of 45 with long hours, poor sleep, missed meals and a great deal of coffee, and every red flag absent. The honest answer stays broad: several causes, none dominant, with a rhythm problem of the heart kept on the list. A learner is most likely to settle on one label too early.

patient.name: Mr David Okafor
patient.manner: Friendly and direct, a little worried, answers plainly.

scenario.opening_words: Thanks, doctor. It's this dizziness. It keeps coming and going and it's starting to worry me a bit.

facts.fact: It feels lightheaded, woozy, as if for a second the ground is not quite solid. Not the room spinning, exactly. Just off.
A spell lasts seconds, sometimes up to a minute. Then it passes and I am fine.
It started about three weeks ago. It is not every day, but a few times a week now.
Sometimes it comes when I stand up from the desk, but sometimes I am just sitting there working.
The room never truly spins. Nothing so strong that I would have to hold on.
I have no ringing in my ears and my hearing is fine.
I have never fainted or blacked out.
I have no chest pain, and I do not notice my heart racing or thumping.
It does not come on with exertion. It comes when I am doing nothing much.
I have no headaches, no double vision, no slurred words, no weakness or numbness, and I walk fine.
Work is brutal, it is year-end. I am doing long hours and sleeping badly.
I often skip lunch and power through on coffee, five or six espressos some days.
I probably do not drink enough water.
I take no medicines at all, nothing new.
I have had no recent injury to my head.

scenario.ideas: I cannot tie it to anything. That is what confuses me.
scenario.concerns: It is starting to worry me. I want to know it is not something serious.
scenario.expectations: I want to know what it is and what to do about it.

differential.diagnosis: Dehydration, missed meals or low blood sugar
Benign positional vertigo or another inner-ear cause

investigations.reason: To look for a postural drop.
To make sure the heart's rhythm is normal.

investigations.investigation: Blood tests: full blood count, glucose or HbA1c, and kidney function
investigations.reason: To look for anaemia, a sugar problem or a kidney problem.

plan.step: Advise water through the day, regular meals and much less coffee
Review with the results of the tests

scenario.safety_net: If it changes: if he faints, has chest pain or a racing heart with it, double vision, slurred speech, weakness, or cannot walk straight, he goes to the emergency department or calls 999 and does not wait.

data_gathering: Ask what the dizziness feels like, and whether the room spins.
Ask about fainting or blacking out.
Ask about chest pain or palpitations with the dizziness.
Ask about double vision, slurred speech, weakness or unsteadiness.
Ask about sleep, meals, coffee and water.
Measure the blood pressure lying and standing.
management: Keep the differential broad and do not settle on one cause.
Keep a heart rhythm problem on the list and do an ECG.
Send a blood count, a glucose and kidney function.
Advise on water, meals and coffee.
Tell him what change would mean going to the emergency department.
relating: Find out that he is worried it is something serious.
Say honestly that the cause cannot be narrowed to one thing yet.
